rules_paraphrased: For base +1 or -1 and exponent +infinity or -infinity, the result is NaN.
Any NaN argument forces a NaN function result, including pow(NaN,0) and pow(1,NaN).
The zero-exponent table covers infinite and signed-zero bases; its always1 entry does not override infectious NaN.
CSS deliberately differs from JavaScript Math.pow(NaN,0).
rust_doc_observation: Official f32::powf examples return1 for powf(NaN,0) and powf(1,NaN); those conflict with CSS infectious NaN.
